<environment_context>
cwd: <CWD>
git: no
entries: README.md, go.mod, internal/
filesystem: read-only (OS-enforced, EACCES on write): <CWD>
filesystem: writable: <TMP>, /home/agent
reads and execution work anywhere; in-tree writes (npm install, go build artifacts, file edits) fail. To run code against this tree, copy it into a writable path first (`cp -a "$PWD" "$TMPDIR/probe"`) - the copy carries go.mod, so language-level rules like Go's internal/ visibility still resolve.
GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE are already redirected to a writable path under $HOME for you, so `go build`/`go test` need no cache setup of your own. GOFLAGS=-mod=mod is also set, so a plain `go build`/`go test` can rewrite go.mod/go.sum as it runs - here it instead fails outright once the module graph needs an update (`go: updating go.mod: ...: permission denied`); pass `-mod=readonly`, or run it against the writable copy above.
Toolchains are installed read-only under /usr - you cannot upgrade one in place; per-project dependencies (pip/npm installs) still go under $HOME. PI_ACP_STATE_DIR is set for you; a tool that derives its own state dir instead of reading that var needs `env -u PI_ACP_STATE_DIR` first.
CI's result, when your task has one, already arrives in the task's envelope - read it there; do not re-run CI's suite just to confirm its verdict.
</environment_context>
